summary: Thomas Roebuck was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the Royal High School. He served as assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St. George (1811) and examiner at Fort William College (~1811–1819).

Thomas Sebeok was a linguist who studied at Magdalene College, the University of Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield, and Princeton University under Roman Jakobson. He spent his career at Indiana University Bloomington (1943–1991), becoming Distinguished Professor Emeritus.
Thomas Seymour Burt worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1821–1823) and served as a Major in the Bengal Engineers from 1824 to 1847.

Thomas Walker Arnold studied at Magdalene College under Edward Byles Cowell. He held posts at Aligarh Muslim University, Government College University, Lahore, University of the Punjab, the India Office, and SOAS University of London as Professor of Arabic and Islamic Studies.

Thomas Watters was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his B.A. from Queen's University Belfast and Queen's University of Ireland (1857–1861). He served in HM Diplomatic Service from 1863 to 1895.

Thomas Welbourne Clark studied at Nottingham, Cambridge, and SOAS under Cyril Alexander Rylands, Ralph Lilley Turner, and Walter Sutton Page. Working in Indology and linguistics, he held lecturing and reader posts at SOAS and visited the University of Pennsylvania.

Thomas Wolseley Haig studied at Wellington College and Sandhurst before working in the Indian Civil Service. In history and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he taught at Trinity College, Hartford (~1923–1925) and SOAS University of London (~1925–1936).
Thomas Zehnder is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Nanking under John Dewey and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He held posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Thubten Chodron studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, and Thubten Zopa Rinpoche. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, she founded and serves as abbess of Sravasti Abbey.

Thubten Jigme Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and as Professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1992).
Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. His students included the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Jigme Norbu, Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa, and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Thubten Samphel was a Tibetologist who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi (~1973–1977), and Columbia University (~1981–1982). He held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Thubten Yeshe studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Rabten, Trijang Rinpoche, and Zong Rinpoche. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he co-founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT, and taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977–1978).

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche studied under Thubten Yeshe, the 14th Dalai Lama, and others. A figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he co-founded Kopan Monastery, founded Maitripa College, and served as spiritual director of the Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition.

Thupten Jinpa studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery, Cambridge, and under the 14th Dalai Lama and Zemey Rinpoche. Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, he held posts at Girton College, Cambridge, and Stanford University, and founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics.
Thupten Tsering is a scholar in the fields of computational studies and Tibetology. He has held academic posts at Tibet University and the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

Thushini S. Jayawardena works in religious studies and other fields. Jayawardena completed a PhD at Auckland University of Technology by 2017 and studied under traditional teacher Satya Narayan Goenka.

Théodore Pavie studied at Lycée David d'Angers and under Eugène Burnouf and Garcin de Tassy. Working in Indology and Sinology, he was Professor of Sanskrit at Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew at the Catholic University of the West (1862).

Thích Minh Châu was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (~1957–1961). He served as lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1955–1964) and Vice Chancellor at Vạn Hạnh University (~1964–1975).
